report: The 50-year-old man has a rapidly growing, painless right scrotal swelling with bloody aspirate. MRI/ultrasound show a multilocular cystic lesion attached to the testis without solid components, contrast enhancement, or testicular abnormality. Pathology reveals bland tall columnar cells without stromal invasion, and IHC is positive for EpCAM/BerEP4 and ER/PR but negative for calretinin, supporting a benign mesothelial/epithelial cystic lesion. T1-hyperintense contents and bloody fluid indicate intralesional hemorrhage. These findings strongly refute malignancy, infection, simple hydrocele, and primary hematocele. Although serum tumor markers are pending and surgical excision is needed for definitive confirmation, the current evidence best supports a benign multilocular paratesticular cystic lesion of mesothelial/epithelial origin with hemorrhage.
